scope: Durable capture and collector/host wiring. Actual disposable files, hardlinks and SQLite; modeled native data and runtime facts.
hash_limit: Scoped after-execution file identities, not a whole-tree attestation.
improvements: Captured bytes and offsets commit atomically; a retry cannot rewrite an earlier chunk.
An old descriptor is drained before a replacement generation is admitted, including unread final bytes.
Restart checks durable prefixes; partial lines, missing old generations, changed bytes and full storage retain failure.
Incremental hashes update only after commit and are reconstructed at restart.
The host checks sealed captures read-only against final archive/alert files.
limitations: No manager, container, VM, network listener or service was started.
The Windows file-handoff test changes the supplied fixed root; actual Linux rename/unlink and Wazuh rotation are unrun.
Input remains a fixed snapshot. Continuous publishing, native recovery, compressed old-generation discovery and the 24-hour run remain unfinished.
No native execution, delivery health or enterprise acceptance is inferred from these checks.
